Among the considered measures, residual $l_1$-norm coherence dominates over the entanglement measures. At very long propagation distances, wave-packet decoherence progressively washes out the oscillatory behavior, driving the oscillation probabilities and quantum correlation measures toward averaged values, with smaller wave-packet widths leading to earlier damping. Further, in the $L-\delta_{\rm CP}$ plane, residual $l_1$-norm coherence exhibits weak $\delta_{\rm CP}$ dependence, while Concurrence Fill and Three-$\pi$ entanglement show greater sensitivity at the DUNE baseline. Beyond a characteristic baseline in the extended propagation regime, all three measures approach constant values, independent of $L$ and $\delta_{\rm CP}$.

item.title: Solar Neutrinos at the ESS{\nu}SB experiment
item.description: arXiv:2611.16807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the sensitivity of the ESSnuSB large underground water-Cherenkov (WC) detector to two key solar neutrino signatures: the MSW spectral upturn in the $^8$B electron neutrino survival probability $P_{ee}(E_\nu)$, and the first direct observation of the rare hep neutrino flux. The analysis incorporates detector systematic uncertainties (energy resolution and flux normalization) and models environmental backgrounds from cosmic-ray muon spallation and $^{222}$Rn contamination. We adopt a shape-driven analysis strategy with a floating overall normalization, so that the discovery power relies on the spectral distortion rather than on the absolute event rate. In a realistic scenario with 90% spallation rejection efficiency, informed by the Super-Kamiokande experience and recent JUNO analyses, residual spallation backgrounds prevent either signal from reaching $5\sigma$ significance within 20 years of exposure. For the hep flux, we present a detailed sensitivity study to both its discovery and its precision, and quantify how the required spallation veto efficiency and recoil energy threshold jointly determine the achievable significance for both signals. At the adopted thresholds, discovery-level sensitivity for both signals requires approximately 99% spallation rejection over a 20-year exposure.

item.title: A unified reduced-mass parametrization of effective chromoelectric interactions in hadrons
item.description: arXiv:2611.16827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a unified effective mass relation in which a common reduced-mass function describes the flavor dependence of chromoelectric pair contributions, with explicit color factors connecting $q\bar q$ and $qq$ pairs. After subtracting fixed spin-weighted chromomagnetic contributions, we jointly fit fourteen spin-averaged meson and baryon masses using constituent quark masses and an additive constant shared by both sectors, obtaining a root-mean-square (RMS) residual of 4 MeV. The fitted saturating form connects the nearly saturated light-flavor contribution with increasing attraction in the heavy-flavor region. In the common saturation limit, the leading chromoelectric contribution acts as a common mass shift for each constituent and can be absorbed into effective constituent masses; the residual pair term accounts for the flavor dependence away from saturation. With the chromomagnetic interaction included, this single parameter set reproduces the ground-state meson and baryon spectra and yields predictions for multiply heavy baryons outside the calibration set. By diagonalizing the sum of the chromoelectric and chromomagnetic mass matrices, we further obtain the ground-state spectra of $cc\bar c\bar c$, $bb\bar b\bar b$, and $bc\bar b\bar c$. The fully charmed tensor mass is ${6505}{(9)(9)}$ MeV, close to recent lattice QCD results, while the upper scalar mass of {${6562}{(9)(12)}$} MeV lies in the mass region near $X(6600)$. The tetraquark masses remain relatively stable under the examined variations of the $qq$ chromomagnetic couplings. The relative $S$-wave rearrangement-decay weights obtained from color--spin recoupling can be used to identify favored decay channels under the stated spatial-overlap approximation.
item.dc:creator: Wen-Nian Liu, Duo-Jie Jia, Fu-Quan Dou

item.title: Dilution of cosmological relics and gravitational waves from a supercooled electroweak phase transition in classically scale-invariant models
item.description: arXiv:2611.16845v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In classically scale-invariant extensions of the Standard Model the electroweak scale is generated radiatively, and the absence of tree-level mass terms keeps the symmetric phase metastable down to very low temperatures. We study the resulting phase transition in a model with a real singlet and several additional scalars coupled to the Higgs doublet and to the singlet, in which electroweak symmetry is broken along a Gildener-Weinberg flat direction and a light dilaton appears in the spectrum. Computing the bounce along the two-dimensional tunnelling path and following the false-vacuum fraction through percolation and completion, we find that the transition proceeds in a single, strongly supercooled step and completes above the QCD scale over a region of parameter space consistent with Higgs measurements and perturbativity. Despite the strong supercooling the transition is fast. The bubble walls reach their terminal velocity early, and almost all of the released vacuum energy goes into bulk motion of the plasma, which thermalises and reheats the universe close to the scale set by the vacuum energy. The resulting entropy injection dilutes pre-existing relics by up to several orders of magnitude. It raises the baryon asymmetry that must be present before the transition, relaxes the unitarity bound on the mass of thermal dark matter, and suppresses earlier gravitational-wave backgrounds. If the acoustic description of gravitational-wave production extends to this regime, the signal peaks in the millihertz band, follows an approximate scaling relation between peak amplitude and frequency set by the vacuum energy, and would be observed by LISA throughout the viable region. The results depend on the multiplicity of the new scalars and their Higgs portal coupling at leading order through a single combination, and require the singlet scale to lie at or above the TeV scale.
item.dc:creator: Arnab Chaudhuri

item.title: Exploring the Pion Vector Form Factor Beyond the Physical Sheet
item.description: arXiv:2611.16974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using analyticity and unitarity, we parametrise the pion vector form factor on the first and second Riemann sheets, below the inelastic $\pi\omega$ threshold. We fit this model-independent parametrisation to the available $\tau^-\to\pi^-\pi^0\nu_\tau$ data from ALEPH, Belle, CLEO and OPAL, together with spacelike data from NA7 and JLab, and extract the pole position and couplings of the $\rho^\pm$ along with the pion charge radius and low-energy $\pi\pi$ scattering parameters. Our results are independent of external scattering input and agree with the literature; in particular, we find $M_{\rho^\pm} = 762.07\pm 0.63$ MeV and $\Gamma_{\rho^\pm} = 143.62^{+0.79}_{-0.80}$ MeV. The parametrisation is publicly available in the EOS software.
item.dc:creator: Florian Herren, Fatemeh Nouri, M\'eril Reboud

item.title: Proton Spin Fluctuation Decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2611.17032v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate a fluctuation decomposition of proton spin in terms of the variances and covariances of the spin and orbital angular momentum of quarks and gluons. We derive their representations in terms of single- and double-parton distributions. The definite proton spin imposes sum rules requiring the variances of its spin and orbital contributions to be compensated by their covariances. This framework reveals correlations and fluctuations that are invisible to the conventional proton spin decomposition.
item.dc:creator: Tomoya Uji

item.title: Nonperturbative Kinetic Description of the Vacuum QGP Production in the Abelian Projection Method
item.description: arXiv:2611.17078v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Within the framework of the Abelian projection method in the $SU(N)$ variant of QCD, a system of nonperturbative selfconsistent equations for the back-reaction problem is derived. This system describes the vacuum production of quarks under the influence of strong quasiclassical gluon fields taking into account violating of the electroneutrality condition.
item.dc:creator: V. V. Dmitriev, S. V. Churochkina, S. A. Smolyansky, V. A. Tseryupa

item.title: Two-loop mixed QCD-EW corrections to bottom-pair production in electron-positron collisions
item.description: arXiv:2611.17171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the two-loop mixed strong-electroweak virtual corrections to the production of a massive bottom-antibottom quark pair in electron-positron collisions. The evaluation of all the relevant Feynman integrals, including those with up to five internal massive lines with three different mass values, has been worked out relying on semi-analytical techniques, using complex-valued masses for the electroweak gauge bosons. The ultraviolet-renormalized and infrared-subtracted finite correction contributes to the NNLO QCD-EW cross section of the inclusive production of a bottom-quark pair. The methodology adopted in this calculation can be extended to the study of fully electroweak second-order corrections to benchmark precision calculations relevant to both the high-luminosity phase of the Large Hadron Collider and prospective future lepton colliders.
item.dc:creator: Simone Devoto, Chinmoy Dey, Michele Dradi, Justin T. Fagnoni, Ziyang Huang, Xinchen Li, Michael J. Ramsey-Musolf, Alessandro Vicini, Jiang Zhu

item.title: Monopole catalysis with massive fermions: the fate of the twisted sector
item.description: arXiv:2611.17253v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the massless limit a fermion scattering on the minimal $SU(5)$ monopole in the lowest partial wave produces an outgoing state with half-integer fermion number in every flavour. This state lives in a twisted sector of the Hilbert space and is now understood as an ordinary fermion attached to a topological line running back to the monopole. In the Standard Model fermion masses and confinement destroy the line at distances greater than the inverse mass scales, causing the twisted state to decay into physical asymptotic states with integer fermion numbers. We study this decay for an incoming lepton or quark of one generation. The cross-section in this partial wave saturates the unitarity bound, $\sigma=\pi/p^2$, and the energy of the outgoing state is shared among the four fermion flavours with a broad Dirichlet distribution, which sets the thresholds and the kinematics. Conservation laws allow exactly two decay channels for each incoming fermion, the helicity flip and its $(B+L)$-violating partner. For an incoming electron the $(B+L)$-violating channel is anti-nucleon synthesis, and we determine the branching ratios in two limits: the two channels are equally likely at high energy, and only the helicity flip remains at low energy, below the anti-nucleon threshold. In between we model the energy dependence. For a quark in a slow proton the $(B+L)$-violating channel is catalysed proton decay, which has no threshold and occurs with a probability close to one. Callan's statistical interpretation of the fractional state emerges in a sharper form: the state is not a superposition of two final states with equal weights, but a single state that decays into them with energy-dependent probabilities, equal only at high energy.
item.dc:creator: Valentin V. Khoze

item.title: A Dark-Sector Mass Flip-Flop Mechanism for the ANITA-IV Events
item.description: arXiv:2611.17328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: ANITA-IV has observed four upward-going air-shower candidates just below the horizon, consistent with ultra-high-energy $\nu_\tau$, yet IceCube, despite its much larger exposure, has detected no neutrino events at such energies. We propose a dark-sector mass flip-flop mechanism that reconciles these observations. We consider an all-sky, monoenergetic flux of ultra-high-energy $N_1$, that is lighter than its partner $N_2$ and stable in vacuum. In our scenario, an ultralight scalar mediating interactions with Earth matter inverts the mass ordering of $N_1$ and $N_2$, allowing an incident $N_1$ to decay into $N_2$ deep underground. The resulting $N_2$ propagates unimpeded through matter and exits the Earth, where the decay $N_2 \to N_1 Z'$ becomes kinematically allowed in the atmosphere, initiating an extensive air shower. At IceCube depths, neither $N_1\to N_2 Z'$ nor $N_2\to N_1 Z'$ is kinematically allowed, which explains the absence of analogous events at IceCube. Normalizing the $N_1$ flux to the four ANITA-IV events, we also predict three events during PUEO's first flight.
item.dc:creator: Dibya S. Chattopadhyay, Carlos A. Arg\"uelles, Vedran Brdar

item.title: A Positive Turn: Coupled Quintessence and Cosmological Neutrino Masses
item.description: arXiv:2611.14584v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In $\Lambda$CDM, the CMB and DESI BAO upper limits on the total neutrino mass are in tension with the lower bounds from oscillation experiments, and analyses allowing negative effective masses favor negative values. We investigate whether a coupled quintessence (CQ) model in which dark matter interacts with a canonical scalar field $\phi$ through an exponential mass coupling $m_{\rm c}(\phi)\propto e^{-\beta\phi/M_{\rm Pl}}$ can alleviate this tension. Combining CMB, DESI, and supernova data, we find that CQ yields neutrino-mass constraints comparable to those obtained in CPL and consistent with oscillation experiments within $2\sigma$ for normal ordering, without requiring the scalar-field equation of state to cross the phantom divide. We further show that it alleviates the tension more effectively than alternative interacting dark energy models that instead favor more negative effective masses. This comparison shows that whether dark sector interactions can relax neutrino mass bounds ultimately depends on the interplay of their effects on primary CMB anisotropies, geometry, growth, and lensing.
item.dc:creator: Tian-Nuo Li, William Giar\`e, Guo-Hong Du, Eleonora Di Valentino, Luis A. Anchordoqui, Shao-Jiang Wang, Xin Zhang, Rong-Gen Cai

item.title: Impact of dynamical, quadratic, and higher-order tidal effects on gravitational-wave observations of binary neutron stars
item.description: arXiv:2611.14628v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neutron-star binaries are prime gravitational-wave sources for current and next-generation detectors, and provide a unique probe for the behaviour of nuclear matter at supranuclear densities. Extracting information about this requires accurate waveform models that capture tidal effects during the late inspiral. We incorporate state-of-the-art tidal corrections into a post-Newtonian inspiral waveform, including dynamical tides and nonlinear contributions from quadratic Love numbers through eighth post-Newtonian (8PN) order. Using Bayesian model comparison, we find that these corrections can significantly affect the gravitational-wave signal, with the 8PN tidal response becoming comparable to lower-PN tidal contributions in the subsolar-mass regime. For exceptionally loud GW170817-like binaries observed by third-generation detectors such as the Einstein Telescope, higher-order tidal effects can be distinguished with high statistical significance, while neglecting them can introduce substantial biases in the inferred tidal deformabilities and, consequently, in constraints on the neutron-star equation of state. These corrections are particularly relevant for putative subsolar-mass binaries: the lower compactness of their constituents enhances tidal effects and makes them potentially important even for current detectors. Our results highlight the importance of higher-order tidal corrections for precision gravitational-wave measurements of dense nuclear matter.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Valletta, Francesco Crescimbeni, Takuya Katagiri, Francesco Pannarale, Paolo Pani

item.title: Benchmarking Machine-Learning Top Taggers from JetClass to a Full-Simulation $Z'\to t\bar{t}$ Search: Transfer, Extrapolation, Sensitivity and Inference Cost
item.description: arXiv:2611.15274v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Searches for heavy resonances decaying to \(t\bar{t}\) test physics beyond the Standard Model at the TeV scale, and their reach depends on how well boosted top jets are identified. Machine-learning top taggers are usually compared on fast-simulation samples without pileup and in a narrow jet-\(p_T\) window, so a benchmark ranking does not directly show how much each tagger adds to a real search. This study trains seven taggers under identical conditions on JetClass. They are a boosted decision tree, two image-based networks, ParticleNet, and three particle transformers (ParT, UParT, and GloParT). The taggers are then applied without retraining to a \(Z'\to t\bar{t}\) search with \(m_{Z'}\) between 1.2 and 2.5~TeV, using 2016 CMS Open Data simulated with Geant4 and realistic pileup. The overall benchmark order of the taggers is preserved. However, taggers with similar area under the ROC curve (AUC) differ by up to a factor of three in jet-level discovery significance. The particle transformers extend the mass reach of the search by \(400~\mathrm{GeV}\), and their lead grows with resonance mass. This gain is seen in fully merged top jets and is associated with stable performance at jet \(p_T\) above the training range. Pileup has only a minor effect on all taggers. A small convolutional network achieves competitive discrimination at a much lower computational cost. The gaps between tagger groups hold under retraining and within statistical uncertainties. The results show that a tagger must be chosen on its kinematic coverage, the working point of the analysis, its discovery sensitivity and its cost, and not on its benchmark score alone.
item.dc:creator: Manisha Kumari, Amal Sarkar

item.title: Constraining Dark Matter Gravitational Production with the 21cm Signal at the Cosmic Dawn
item.description: arXiv:2611.15454v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The origin of dark matter is one of the major problems in modern cosmology. We can infer its existence from the gravitational potential wells around astrophysical objects, but there is no convincing explanation for what its nature and origin are. Moreover, experiments for direct detection, indirect detection, or particle production in accelerators have not shown, until now, any conclusive interaction between dark matter and particles in the standard model. This may imply that dark matter does not interact with ordinary matter and originates from pure gravitational interaction. In this manuscript, we investigate the possibility to constrain the gravitational production of dark matter from the 21cm brightness temperature at the cosmic dawn. Considering only the time when the absorption profile occurs, we can impose upper limits on the dark matter's mass. Future measurements have potential to extend current constraints and help understanding the nature of dark matter.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'e A. Costa, Valdir B. Bezerra

item.title: Enhanced Early Structure from Axiodilatons & 21cm Observations
item.description: arXiv:2611.15647v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Axiodilatons provide a promising unified model of the Dark Sector whose properties are motivated by the use of accidental approximate symmetries to embed the light fields needed for observations into well-motivated UV physics in a technically natural way. These models turn out to help ameliorate many current puzzles in $\Lambda$CDM phenomenology (e.g. the Hubble tension and the evidence for evolving Dark Energy) `for free' despite not being designed for that purpose. We here explore in more detail another serendipitous feature of these models: their tendency to enhance early structure formation, in a way that seems suggestive given the accumulating evidence for structure arising earlier than expected in $\Lambda$CDM. Since early structure growth is the cleanest to study we explore in detail the expected 21cm signal produced by axiodilaton models, using the same parameter choices that improve agreement with observations elsewhere in cosmology. For fixed astrophysics, we forecast that SKA1-Low could distinguish dilaton couplings as small as a few times $10^{-2}$ from $\Lambda$CDM at $2\sigma$, mainly because of the earlier formation of structure. We provide complete derivations of the mass dependence of the relevant cosmological observables, including how dilaton-dependent baryon and electron masses affect the hyperfine transition, the Ly$\alpha$ coupling, X-ray heating and ionization during cosmic dawn and the epoch of reionization. We provide details of radiative transfer, atomic physics and the equations governing the thermal and ionization state of the intergalactic medium.
item.dc:creator: Chan Youn Weon, Carsten van de Bruck, C. P. Burgess, Jeong Han Kim, Adam Smith

item.title: Triple-Massive-Exchange Bispectrum of Quasi-Single-Field Inflation
item.description: arXiv:2611.15660v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The triple-exchange bispectrum of the scalar quasi-single-field inflation model has resisted analytic evaluation across its full parameter space since its advent, despite rapid progress in cosmological collider physics. In this Letter, we solve it for general mass and mixing strength as a convergent double series, by applying the Mellin-Barnes representation directly to the mixed propagator between the massless and massive modes. The result is exact, non-perturbative, and physically transparent; the method is broadly applicable.
item.dc:creator: Xingang Chen, Zhong-Zhi Xianyu

item.title: Cosmological Signals from Finite-Lifetime Domain Wall Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.15860v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study cosmological perturbations sourced by metastable domain wall (DW) networks. Using the unconnected segment model, we derive analytic expressions for the scalar and tensor power spectra in the long-wavelength regime, finding a fixed ratio between their amplitudes during the scaling regime. These spectra grow as the network evolves, driven by the increasing correlation length and slower redshifting of the wall energy density relative to radiation, and peak at a scale set by the network's collapse time. Comparing the scalar spectrum with observational constraints, we derive bounds on the DW energy density at collapse, which we apply to $\mathbb{Z}_2$ and axion models. When these bounds are saturated, the resulting CMB $B$-mode signal can be comparable to or larger than the inflationary signal for a tensor-to-scalar ratio $r \sim 0.03$, potentially bringing it within reach of future CMB polarization experiments.
item.dc:creator: Fengwei Yang, Kylar Greene, Aurora Ireland, Yuhsin Tsai

item.title: Gray-body factors: Method matters II, WKB vs GrayHawk
item.description: arXiv:2611.15889v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a systematic comparison between two independent approaches for the computation of gray-body factors. A fully numerical integration of the radial scattering equation, as implemented in GrayHawk, and one based on the WKB approximation. We consider four black hole geometries and scalar, fermionic, and vector perturbations, comparing the corresponding gray-body factors, primary Hawking emission spectra, and Page evaporation factors. As expected for high-frequency and large $l$ regimes, the two methods provide excellent agreement. At low frequencies, however, systematic discrepancies emerge and become particularly pronounced for nearly-extremal black holes. Systematic discrepancies are also met when considering effective geometric potentials characterized by the presence of more than one peak. A significant difference between the two approaches is also found in their computational cost, highlighting their complementary nature.
item.dc:creator: Marco Calz\`a, Andrea Spina

item.title: Strangeness in the Chiral Mean Field model phase diagram
item.description: arXiv:2611.15894v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We explore the phase diagram of the Chiral Mean Field model in the space of temperature and baryon, charge, and strangeness chemical potentials, focusing on the role of the strangeness direction. At low density, a negative $\mu_S$ leads to finite strangeness in the nuclear liquid--gas transition and rotates the order parameter away from the purely baryonic direction. The critical mode remains baryon dominated over the $\mu_S$ range considered, while the critical locus develops a strong parametrization dependence once multistrange baryons appear. At higher density, a separate first-order transition toward strangeness-rich hadronic matter appears only for one of the two parametrizations considered, emphasizing its interaction dependence. The high density transition reorganizes octet-dominated matter into decuplet-dominated matter: $\Delta$ baryons provide most of the baryon-density discontinuity, while $\Xi^*(1530)$ baryons provide the largest contribution to the strangeness-density discontinuity. Its order parameter is dominated by the strangeness density, and its normalized direction in the $BQS$ space changes little with temperature even as the discontinuity vanishes at the critical point. The critical baryon chemical potential changes by almost $1$~GeV over $\mu_S\in [-300, 300]$~MeV. We characterize both transitions using the fixed-temperature $BQS$ susceptibility matrix, the density discontinuity between the coexisting phases, and a generalized Clausius--Clapeyron relation. This work also accompanies the release of \cmfpp{} \texttt{v2.0.0} as part of the MUSES framework. The extension of the initial release includes, among other features, finite-temperature thermodynamics, new interactions and parametrizations, and susceptibility calculations based on a Jacobian method.
item.dc:creator: Mateus Reinke Pelicer, Nikolas Cruz-Camacho, Rajesh Kumar, Veronica Dexheimer, Jaquelyn Noronha-Hostler

item.title: Magnetic-slope crossovers in the QCD bulk-to-shear viscosity ratio
item.description: arXiv:2611.15929v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How a magnetic field alters dissipation in quark--gluon matter is almost unconstrained from first principles, since real-time transport is not directly accessible to lattice simulation. Using a top-down MQGP-inspired M/string-theory construction of a QCD-like thermal plasma, together with a kinetic-theory identity within a specified single-mode quasiparticle truncation and a compatibility construction using available lattice equation-of-state data, we propose a normalization-insensitive sign prediction that the field slope of the longitudinal bulk-to-shear viscosity ratio \zeta_\parallel/\eta_\parallel reverses sign twice with temperature---below and above the deconfinement pseudo-critical temperature T_0, at T_1<T_0<T_2 (the lower reversal T_1 conditional on a stated pion-gas rate inequality). A kinetic-theory identity with phase-appropriate carriers, a quark--gluon plasma above T_0 and a chiral pion gas below, reproduces the same pattern, and lattice speed-of-sound data can be shown to be consistent as well. The bottom-up VQCD in the deconfined phase supports a negative slope for large temperatures; the slope crossover is not resolvable from the available \zeta_\parallel/s, \eta_\parallel/s plots.
item.dc:creator: Aalok Misra, Shivam S. Kushwah, Keshav Dasgupta, Charles Gale, Sangyong Jeon

item.title: Silent Heavy Fields: An Exclusion Rule for the Cosmological Collider
item.description: arXiv:2611.16029v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The cosmological collider uses oscillatory signatures in primordial correlators to probe heavy fields during inflation. This probe has blind spots, as heavy fields can keep ticking in time while remaining silent in the correlators. In this letter, we derive an exclusion rule under which cosmological collider signals vanish. The rule covers two classes of diagrams where a de Sitter invariant heavy sector couples covariantly to a single external field at one vertex. We first prove it for exchanges mediated by the two-point function of the heavy sector to all loop orders, using a spectral decomposition followed by a field redefinition. The result then extends to one-loop polygons by matching their oscillatory contributions onto those of the first class. The approximate signals of previously studied processes that fall into these classes must therefore be revisited. As a nonvanishing example, we derive the leading signal of a triangle loop for the first time in a toy model motivated by chemical potentials.
item.dc:creator: Shuntaro Aoki, Zhehan Qin, Masahide Yamaguchi, Yuhang Zhu

item.title: Anti-periodic Gravitino and Dirac Effective Operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.16047v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Introducing a preserved $U(1)_R$ symmetry forbids gravitini Majorana masses while allowing a Dirac mass. We investigate how a Dirac mass for gravitini can be described by an effective operator in $N=1$ superspace, in analogy with the well-known Dirac gaugino mass. We find that the corresponding spin-$3/2$ bilinear operator can be expressed in terms of gauge-invariant gravitino curvature superfields coupled through a nonlocal kernel involving an inverse d'Alembertian. We study this construction in minimal five-dimensional supergravity compactified on $S^1/\mathbb Z_2$. The gravitino satisfies anti-periodic boundary conditions induced by a Scherk-Schwarz twist. The physical Kaluza-Klein Dirac masses then appear as poles in the two-point functions of the curvature superfields associated with sources localized at the endpoints. Separation of physical and gauge modes relates these propagators to a quadratic fermionic kernel represented by a $16\times16$ matrix. Its elements match the fermionic components of two invariants written in $N=1$ superspace, including their spinor contractions and normalization. This matching is carried out on a fixed background with a nonzero radion auxiliary field.
item.dc:creator: Karim Benakli

item.title: Recurrent Fourier Neural Operator for Event-by-Event Relativistic Hydrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.16511v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Relativistic hydrodynamics is a powerful tool to simulate the evolution of the quark--gluon plasma (QGP) in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, but event-by-event simulations are computationally demanding, especially for Bayesian analyses. We develop a recurrent Fourier neural operator (rFNO) that emulates the evolution of $(2+1)$-dimensional relativistic hydrodynamics. Three networks are trained on the $32\times32$, $64\times64$, and $128\times128$ lattices using profiles of the same \textsc{VISH2+1} hydrodynamic events up to $\tau-\tau_0=4.8~\mathrm{fm}/c$. The networks trained on the coarser lattices are then directly evaluated on the $128\times128$ lattice without retraining, while the $128\times128$ network provides the native-resolution reference. A comparison with the \textsc{VISH2+1} results shows that the rFNO predictions across resolutions nicely capture the magnitude and structures of the temperature profiles, and describe the event-by-event eccentricities $\varepsilon_n$ ($n=2,3,4$), the momentum anisotropy $\varepsilon_p$, and their time evolution within the supervised proper-time interval. After the recurrent continuation to $\tau-\tau_0=6.4~\mathrm{fm}/c$, the relative errors of the predicted $\varepsilon_n$ and $\varepsilon_p$ remain within about $10\%$. These results demonstrate that the rFNO realizes zero-shot super-resolution predictions for relativistic hydrodynamics and can be recurrently continued beyond the supervised interval.
item.dc:creator: Xiangrun Bao, Lingxiao Wang, Huichao Song

item.title: Matching lattice and continuum chiral determinants at finite volume
item.description: arXiv:2611.16544v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent formulations of lattice chiral gauge theories define a complex fermion weight either through Craig's gauge-invariant overlap measure or, following Hsu and Witten, through a continuum Weyl determinant on a reconstructed gauge connection, with its phase fixed by the five-dimensional $\eta$-invariant. For one $SU(5)$ generation on a flat four-torus, we prove that their relative weights agree in the continuum limit along smooth gapped paths, after fixing a normalization and subtracting a local Yang-Mills counterterm, whose coefficient we determine. On bounded smooth families a uniform Dirac gap suffices: the vacuum expansion need not converge. We obtain explicit uniform convergence rates for the logarithmic variations and, for Craig's interpolation, prove the reconstruction bounds that the matching requires, extending Hsu's small-field comparison to finite amplitude. For Hsu's reflection-positive reconstruction with flat collars, the phase variations still match, while the logarithmic coefficient of the quadratic counterterm is enhanced by a calculable, profile-dependent factor. In a hypercharge background on which the vacuum expansion diverges, numerical comparisons at the input gauge field support quadratic convergence of the phase, whereas the modulus acquires a logarithmic correction to quadratic scaling, whose coefficient follows analytically from the free overlap vacuum polarization.
item.dc:creator: Zhengwen Liu

item.title: Is Spin Slow in Hot QCD?
item.description: arXiv:2611.16684v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Promoting spin to a hydrodynamic variable requires slow relaxation, as mass-suppressed helicity flips in hot QCD suggest. Using the full leading-order collision operator, we show instead that light-quark spin damps at the transport rate $g^4T\ln(1/g)$, nearly as fast as vector currents. Since spatial spin locks to momentum, helicity-conserving soft, small-angle scatterings readily rotate it. Damping involves multiple kinetic modes beyond a single relaxation time, global rotation adds only reversible precession, and stronger coupling further disfavors a slow spin mode in quark-gluon plasma.
item.dc:creator: Zi-Hao Liu, Mei Huang

item.title: Resolving Radiogenic Heterogeneity in the Earth's Mantle with Multi-Site Geo-neutrino Measurements
item.description: arXiv:2611.16715v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a global fit to geo-neutrino measurements at four underground sites (Kamioka, Gran Sasso, Sudbury, Jiangmen), combining signal rates with site-specific predictions of the lithospheric contribution to constrain the quantity and distribution of radioactivity in the Earth's mantle. Assuming a uniform distribution of radioactivity in the mantle, we find a geo-neutrino rate of $S_\text{mantle} = 14.8 \pm 4.5$ NIU when the lithospheric predictions are allowed to vary within their uncertainties. This uniform mantle signal rate corresponds to radiogenic heating of $18.5 \pm 5.6$ TW. Although the uniform-mantle signal is resolved at $\sim3.2\sigma$, there is noticeable tension between the inferred mantle signals at Jiangmen and Kamioka, which may indicate non-uniform geo-neutrino production in the mantle. We explore six families of models to describe the heterogeneous spatial distribution of radiogenic elements in the Earth's mantle. Each model contains anomalous bodies or reservoirs carrying an excess of heat-producing elements over a depleted mantle (DM) background, with total inventory set by bulk-silicate-Earth mass balance and by a geochemical Th/U constraint. For each model, we compute the geo-response at each detector site and fit the resulting signals to the four measurements. A total of 968,274 individual model configurations are defined and tested. The results of $\sim$3 million distinct fits show that no plausible mantle or lithosphere model applied uniformly to all four sites reproduces the difference between the inferred mantle signals at the Jiangmen and Kamioka sites. Only local, site-specific prescriptions are able to reach the observed difference, suggesting that the Kamioka-Jiangmen tension is due to a local effect or statistical scatter, rather than large-scale mantle structure.
item.dc:creator: Michael Leyton, Stephen T. Dye

item.title: Bayesian Inference of Fermionic Dark Matter Admixed Neutron Stars Informed by Galaxy Cluster Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2611.16785v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Self-interacting dark matter is constrained on galactic and cluster scales by its elastic scattering cross section per unit mass, $\sigma/m_\chi \sim 0.1-10\ {\rm cm^2/g}$. We incorporate this cross section into the equation of state of an asymmetric, self-interacting fermionic dark matter component and perform a Bayesian inference of dark matter admixed neutron stars in the two-fluid framework at $\sigma/m_\chi = 0.1$, $1$ and $10\ {\rm cm^2/g}$. Seven nuclear matter parameters are sampled together with the dark particle mass and mass fraction, and confronted with nuclear theory and neutron star observations. The nuclear sector and the global observables are statistically indistinguishable across the whole range of cross sections, while the data constrain the dark matter mass to $m_\chi \simeq 1.45-1.88$~GeV and its mass fraction to $f_\chi \simeq 0.05-0.09$, depending on the cross section. Finally, comparing runs built from the same parameter draws, so that only the cross section differs, we find that it does change the baryonic radius appreciably, but only for light dark matter, a region the astrophysical data largely disfavor. The self-interaction is therefore not too weak to be seen; however its effect is hidden in the region of parameter space that the present observational data already disfavor.
item.dc:creator: H. C. Das, J. B. Wei

item.title: Gauge Theory Bootstrap with varying $N_c$
item.description: arXiv:2611.16824v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use the Gauge Theory Bootstrap to study asymptotically free gauge theories with a varying number of colors $N_c$. The parameter $N_c$ enters the computation through the sum rules and asymptotic form factors, allowing us to tune this microscopic parameter directly and examine the corresponding low-energy strongly coupled dynamics. For $3\le N_c\le 12$, we extract the scattering lengths, effective ranges, and low-energy constants $\bar{l}_i$, and study their $N_c$ dependence. We also obtain the $\sigma$, $\rho$, and $f_2$ resonances for the same range of $N_c$. The $\rho$ and $f_2$ masses depend only weakly on $N_c$, and their widths decrease as $N_c$ increases, consistent with the $1/N_c$ scaling expected for conventional $q\bar{q}$ mesons. In contrast, the $\sigma$ meson mass and width both increase with $N_c$, in agreement with a previous unitarized $\chi$PT analysis. These results provide a further test of the Gauge Theory Bootstrap for studying asymptotically free gauge theories.
item.dc:creator: Rafael Cordoba, Yifei He, Martin Kruczenski, Derek Ping, Jignesh Mohanty, Emil Alegria

item.title: Why magnetic-field effects are difficult to observe in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
item.description: arXiv:2611.16904v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Since a strong magnetic field is generated in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, novel phenomena have been predicted to occur in the quark-gluon plasma produced in these collisions. However, these predictions have not yet been convincingly confirmed experimentally. We reanalyze the generation and evolution of the magnetic field which plays a key role in the phenomena. Using the method of one-sided Fourier transformation, we reconcile the description in frequency and wave-vector space, which is required to properly account for the electromagnetic properties of the quark-gluon plasma, with the initial-value nature of the problem arising from the creation of the plasma medium at the moment of collision. We show that the currents induced in the quark-gluon plasma, which sustain the magnetic field, develop with a delay and are consequently less effective than usually assumed. Moreover, because the plasma initially consists predominantly of electrically neutral gluons, while charged quarks emerge at a later stage, the induced currents are further delayed. Consequently, a magnitude of the field present in the quark-gluon plasma is significantly lower than earlier estimates suggested. This may explain why magnetic-field effects are difficult to observe in relativistic heavy-ion collisions.
item.dc:creator: Stanislaw Mrowczynski, Maciej Pylak

item.title: Quantitative Junction Transport Modeling of RHIC Charge and Baryon Stopping
item.description: arXiv:2611.16977v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Charge and baryon stopping in Ru+Ru and Zr+Zr isobar collisions are modeled by HIJING with junction. With realistic nuclear geometry and a tuned diquark splitting, it reproduces STAR's net-baryon yield, charge difference, and scaled baryon-to-charge ratio at midrapidity. Junctions set the ratio's magnitude while neutron skins drive its centrality trend. At the LHC, large asymmetric pair production in HIJING obscures junction effects, causing apparent tension with data. This tuned generator reproduces RHIC data and predicts O+O behavior, setting a quantitative benchmark for baryon transport.
item.dc:creator: Ashish Pandav, Zhangbu Xu, Bedangadas Mohanty

item.title: Three-body dynamics of the Roper resonance
item.description: arXiv:2611.17139v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The enigmatic Roper resonance is notoriously difficult to determine in lattice QCD. Its quantum numbers, $J^P=1/2^+$, allow for two pions and a nucleon in relative $S$-waves. This absence of a centrifugal barrier leads to strong three-body $\pi\pi N$ effects on top of the two-body $\pi N$ channel -maybe the reason why the Roper is obscured in lattice QCD close to physical masses. Guided by unitarity, an amplitude is constructed in which three-body states are populated through channels in $f_0(500)N(939)1/2^+$, $\pi\Delta(1232)3/2^+$, and $\pi N(1440)1/2^+$ configurations. The latter channel is required by unitarity in the presence of nucleon exchange, and it contains the nucleon as a bound state, generating the $\pi N$ channel automatically. With the sub-channels matching the corresponding two-body amplitudes from experiment and nucleon properties, the $P_{11}$ amplitude from SAID is fitted, allowing for an accurate determination of the Roper poles close to the complex $\pi\Delta$ threshold. The Roper poles and residues are, for the first time, determined by explicitly including this and other non-analyticities in combination with strict two- and three-body unitarity. Contour deformation allows for a direct pole search. Systematic uncertainties from the parametrization dependence are quantified. The result for the Roper $S$-matrix pole is $\sqrt{s_R}/{\rm MeV} =1346\pm 2^{+6}_{-3} - i(81\pm 2^{+7}_{-8})$. The amplitude developed here will serve as the central input for a quantization condition that allows for future determinations of the Roper resonance from lattice QCD.
item.dc:creator: Jinzi Wu, Michael D\"oring, Maxim Mai

item.title: Probing Ultralight Higher-spin Dark Matter using Stellar Kinematics of Dwarf Galaxies
item.description: arXiv:2611.17204v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stellar kinematics of the classical Milky Way dwarf galaxies provide a powerful probe of the dark matter distribution and its underlying physics. In this article we use them to explore ultralight dark matter (ULDM) with a non-zero spin. Numerical simulations in the non-relativistic limit have shown that, for the same initial conditions, higher-spin ULDM forms a more diffuse soliton core at the galactic center, with a smoother transition to the NFW outer region, than scalar ULDM. We introduce a generalized parametrization of the ULDM halo profile that captures these spin-induced effects through three additional parameters: the normalization of the central core density, the exponent of the core-halo mass relation, and the radius of the transition to the NFW envelope. Applying this profile in a Bayesian analysis of six classical dwarf galaxies, we find halo masses in the range $10^{8.5}$-$10^{9.5}\,M_\odot$ and, from each galaxy individually, a particle mass $m \gtrsim 3\times10^{-21}$ eV. The core-halo exponent and the transition radius are consistent with their scalar values. The core-density normalization is also consistent with the scalar value in four galaxies and prefers a core denser than a scalar soliton in Fornax, while the factor-of-several suppression expected for higher-spin cores is not excluded by any single galaxy. The data therefore show no preference for the more diffuse cores of higher-spin ULDM, but do not yet rule them out.
item.dc:creator: Praniti Singh, JiJi Fan, Savvas M. Koushiappas, Isabelle S. Goldstein

item.title: The Higgs boson as a self-similar system: Tsallis form factors and the electroweak hierarchy problem
item.description: arXiv:2204.09916v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the electroweak hierarchy problem for a composite Higgs boson with a statistically self-similar internal structure. Using the spectral representation of the Higgs propagator, we show that this structure can contribute only through momentum-dependent vertex functions. In a superstatistical model of the self-similar structure, a Gamma-distributed size of the constituents turns a Gaussian vertex form factor into the $q$-exponential (Tsallis) form factor $F_q(k_E^2)=[1+(q-1)k_E^2/M^2]^{-1/(q-1)}$, where $M$ is the compositeness scale and $q-1=2/(3N)$ for an effective number $N$ of constituents. These form factors interpolate between those of nonlocal field theories ($q\to1$) and Lee--Wick-type models ($q=2$). For $1<q<2$ every one-loop contribution to the Higgs mass is finite and heavy states decouple. For the benchmarks $q=11/9$, $4/3$ and $5/3$, tuning is negligible ($\Delta\lesssim1$) for $M$ up to about $1$--$2$~TeV, and remains mild ($\Delta \leq 10$) for $M$ up to about $3$--$5$~TeV. The hierarchy problem is thus converted into the requirement of new composite dynamics near the TeV scale, testable at the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider through off-shell and high-momentum Higgs processes and searches for new states near $M$.
item.dc:creator: M. Ahmadvand

item.title: Stellar evolution and axion-like particles: new constraints and hints from globular clusters in the GAIA DR3 data
item.description: arXiv:2410.02266v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Axion-like particles (ALPs) are hypothetical pseudoscalar bosons, natural in extensions of the Standard Model. Their interactions with ordinary matter and radiation are suppressed, making it challenging to detect them in laboratory experiments. However, these particles, produced within stellar interiors, can provide an additional mechanism for energy loss, potentially influencing stellar evolution. Prominent methods for searching for such effects involve measuring the properties of red giants and helium-burning stars in globular clusters (GCs). Here we use published catalogs of stars selected as members of seven GCs on the basis of parallaxes and proper motions measured by Gaia (Data Release 3). Making use of previously derived theoretical relations and the new data, we find the upper limit on the ALP-electron coupling, g_{ae}<1.3*10^{-13} (95% CL), and an indication (2.6 sigma) to nonzero ALP-photon coupling, g_{a\gamma}=(6.6+1.3-1.8)*10^{-11} GeV^{-1}. Given the precision of contemporary observational data, it is imperative to refine ALP constraints through more sophisticated analyses, which will be explored in detail elsewhere.
item.dc:creator: S. V. Troitsky

item.title: Generating the Dark Matter mass from the QCD vacuum: A new approach to the mass aspect of the Dark Matter-Baryon coincidence problem
item.description: arXiv:2411.18725v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The comparable abundances of dark matter and baryons imply a deep connection between the dark sector and the QCD sector. In asymmetric dark matter models, the number densities of both sectors are ensured to be similar. However, a complete solution should also include a mechanism relating their masses. In this study, we explore a new mechanism where an $\mathcal{O}(\Lambda_{\rm QCD})$ dark matter mass arises from the QCD vacuum. The idea is realized by a strongly coupled chiral dark sector, featuring a light composite fermion as the dark matter. Its mass is generated through the vacuum misalignment induced by QCD, ensuring the mass to be comparable with baryons. The model also features additional light bosons, including GeV-scale dark pions and a composite QCD axion.
item.dc:creator: Yi Chung

item.title: Space-time Areas and Hadronization Studies
item.description: arXiv:2508.05784v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Space-time area laws play a fundamental role in modeling strongly interacting phenomena, such as in relativistic string models, QCD on the lattice, and in hadronization modeling. For the latter, an exact expression for relevant space-time areas related to the final state hadronic events for hadrons of any mass is calculated. Usage of this expression in the UCLA hadronization model helps validate its space-time area law (STAL) principle and unifies the treatment of heavy and light hadrons via a single fragmentation function.
item.dc:creator: S. Abachi, C. Buchanan

item.title: Reevaluating the $a_1(1420)$ enhancement and its molecular partners in the low-lying axial-vector meson spectrum
item.description: arXiv:2512.02655v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate possible axial-vector poles associated with the near-threshold $K^{\ast}\bar K$ interaction, driven by the Weinberg-Tomozawa term and unitarized through the Bethe-Salpeter equation. In the isovector sectors with $I^G(J^{PC})=1^\pm(1^{+\mp})$, we find second-sheet poles below the $K^{\ast}\bar K$ threshold and examine their possible manifestations in the $a_1(1420)$ structure and its possible partner $b_1(1400)$. The corresponding $f_0(980)\pi$ and $\phi\pi$ invariant-mass distributions are compared with the COMPASS and BESIII data, respectively. Within the present framework, the enhancements around 1.4 GeV may be qualitatively understood through the interplay between the triangle-singularity mechanism and the pole-enhanced $K^\ast\bar K$ final-state interaction, although a quantitative description requires a more complete treatment of coupled channels and production dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Mao-Jun Yan, Chun-Sheng An, Cheng-Rong Deng

item.title: New Type of Monopoles in QCD and Standard Model
item.description: arXiv:2512.08234v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present the new monopole solutions in QCD, the Georgi-Glashow model, and the standard model. QCD has a new monopole, the Wu-Yang monopole which has the chromon dressing. The Georgi-Glashow model has a new monopole, the Wu-Yang monopole which has the W boson dressing, in addition to the well-known 'tHooft-Polyakov monopole. Moreover, the standard model has two types of monopoles, the well known Cho-Maison type monopoles which carry the magnetic charge $4\pi/e$ and the electromagnetically neutral type of magnetic monopoles (the naked one and the one with the W boson dressing) which carry the neutral magnetic charge $4\pi/\bae$, where $\bae$ is the neutral charge. We show how to construct the new monopole solutions and clarify the topological origin of the new monopoles. The new monopoles could have deep implications not just in high energy physics but also in condensed matter physics.
item.dc:creator: Liping Zou, Pengming Zhang, Y. M. Cho

item.title: Heavy Neutrinos across the Electroweak-to-Multi-TeV Frontier via Novel ML-Enhanced Probes
item.description: arXiv:2601.09095v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a new strategy to probe heavy neutrinos with non-universal fermion couplings at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) using a novel production mechanism and machine-learning algorithms. Focusing on proton--proton collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13.6~\mathrm{TeV}$, we investigate final states containing a charged lepton, missing transverse energy, and two jets. For heavy neutrino masses below $\mathcal{O}(1~\mathrm{TeV})$, production is dominated by the $s$ channel process. At higher masses, vector boson fusion becomes the dominant production mechanism, with cross sections that decrease slowly as the heavy neutrino mass increases. We simulate both signal and Standard Model background events and employ gradient-boosted decision trees to optimize event classification. Assuming an integrated luminosity of $3000~\mathrm{fb^{-1}}$, expected for the high-luminosity, and considering realistic statistical and systematic uncertainties, we find that heavy neutrinos in the mass range $50~\mathrm{GeV}$--$10~\mathrm{TeV}$ can be probed with sensitivity to the mixing parameter $|V_{\ell N}|^2$ spanning from $\mathcal{O}(10^{-5})$ to 1. This approach enhances the discovery potential for heavy neutrinos and provides a complementary pathway to existing search strategies.
item.dc:creator: Yin-Fa Shen, Alfredo Gurrola, Francesco Romeo, Denis Rathjens, Andres Fl\'orez

item.title: Fluctuation-Induced Backreaction on Bubble-Wall Dynamics in Cosmological First-Order Phase Transitions
item.description: arXiv:2602.04586v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study bubble-wall dynamics in cosmological first-order phase transitions in a two-scalar-field model, where the wall is formed by the scalar field $\phi$ and an additional real scalar field $s$ is coupled to it through a portal interaction. We evolve the coupled classical field equations on the lattice and consider a prescribed classical stochastic background of $s$ fluctuations at the onset of the phase transition. Through the portal interaction, this patchy background intermittently modulates the local driving pressure on the wall. The wall consequently undergoes alternating episodes of acceleration and deceleration, with a smaller finite-time averaged propagation rate than in the decoupled limit. A wall-frame analysis of the dynamical $s$-sector energy reveals a coupling-dependent crossover from excess energy deposited behind the wall at weak coupling to a front-side bias at strong coupling. These results demonstrate an additional scalar-field source of bubble-wall backreaction and may affect gravitational-wave and baryogenesis predictions.
item.dc:creator: Dongdong Wei, Zong-Kuan Guo

item.title: MadNIS at NLO
item.description: arXiv:2603.22407v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We combine fast amplitude surrogates with neural importance sampling to accelerate NLO calculations. For virtual corrections, a learned ratio to the Born matrix element with calibrated uncertainties guarantees reliable precision across phase space. For real emission, we stick to the standard FKS subtraction and train sector-conditioned surrogates of the regularized integrands away from divergences. MadNIS then uses multi-channel mappings and FKS sectors as conditions. We validate our approach for electron-positron scattering to three and four jets and find significant speed-ups and variance reduction in the integration.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni De Crescenzo, Javier Mari\~no Villadamigo, Nina Elmer, Theo Heimel, Tilman Plehn, Ramon Winterhalder, Marco Zaro

item.title: Bag Parameters for Heavy Meson Lifetimes from a Lattice QCD Calculation at the SU(3)$_{\rm F}$-symmetric Point
item.description: arXiv:2603.28516v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We calculate the dimension-six $\Delta Q=0$ four-quark matrix elements describing heavy-meson lifetime ratios using the gradient flow with its short flow-time expansion as a renormalization procedure. On six RBC/UKQCD 2+1-flavor domain-wall fermion ensembles, we determine flowed bag parameters for physical charm and strange quarks and match to the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ scheme with perturbative short flow-time expansion coefficients through next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO). A multiscale matching procedure using renormalization-group running improves the extrapolation to zero flow time. For the operators relevant to $\tau(D_s)/\tau(D^0)$ at the SU(3)$_{\rm F}$ symmetric point, we obtain $B_1^{\overline{\text{MS}}}(3\,{\rm GeV})=1.0524(97)$,$B_2^{\overline{\text{MS}}}(3\,{\rm GeV})=0.9621(70)$, $\epsilon_1^{\overline{\text{MS}}}(3\,{\rm GeV})=-0.2275(76)$, and $\epsilon_2^{\overline{\text{MS}}}(3\,{\rm GeV})=-0.0005(8)$ using a specific choice of evanescent operators. This is the first lattice-QCD determination of $\Delta Q=0$ four-quark operators with a full error budget. It opens the path towards higher-precision predictions of heavy-meson lifetimes and similar quantities exhibiting operator mixing under renormalization.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Black, Robert V. Harlander, Jonas T. Kohnen, Fabian Lange, Antonio Rago, Andrea Shindler, Oliver Witzel

item.title: Squeezed double-$b$ tagging for light hadronic resonances at the LHC
item.description: arXiv:2604.06937v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A boosted light resonance decaying into $b\bar b$ can produce a single jet containing two bottom-hadron decay systems. We investigate this squeezed double-$b$ topology using a tracking-based boosted decision tree that distinguishes non-bottom, single-bottom and double-bottom jets. The classifier combines displaced-track multiplicities and momentum fractions with ordered impact parameters and jet kinematics. For the simulated jet samples, the double-bottom tagging response is approximately $83\%$, with corresponding single-bottom and non-bottom mistag responses of $9.7\%$ and $0.5\%$; charm contamination is assessed separately. The tagger is combined with soft-drop mass reconstruction and an event-level classifier using the candidate and recoil jets to identify light hadronic resonances within the QCD background. As an illustrative example, we consider a singlet extension of the flipped two-Higgs-doublet model with pseudoscalar masses of 30, 50 and 60 GeV. The signal samples use a simplified effective-vertex approximation, replacing the momentum-dependent quark-loop production interaction by a local vertex. A resolved loop calculation and higher-order production corrections are beyond the scope of this tagging study. The resulting reconstruction strategy can be applied to different signal hypotheses with their corresponding kinematic acceptance and tagging response.
item.dc:creator: Dilip Kumar Ghosh, Biswarup Mukhopadhyaya, Sirshendu Samanta, Ritesh K. Singh

item.title: Heavy Quark Transport is Non-Gaussian Beyond Leading Log
item.description: arXiv:2604.21895v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We find that heavy quark transport beyond leading logarithm at weak coupling is intrinsically non-Gaussian: the longitudinal momentum transfer distribution has asymmetric exponential tails that are crucial for equilibration dynamics. We show this by computing the leading-order momentum transfer kernel for relativistic heavy quarks in weakly coupled non-Abelian plasmas, matching perturbative momentum transfer on the thermal scale to hard-thermal-loop-resummed soft physics. This is the same structure previously found in strongly coupled holographic plasmas, showing that it is not peculiar to weak or strong coupling, conformality, or supersymmetry. We therefore expect that this is a robust feature that physical quark-gluon plasma should also exhibit.
item.dc:creator: Jean F. Du Plessis, Bruno Scheihing-Hitschfeld

item.title: Collisional energy loss distribution of a fast parton in a hot or dense QCD medium
item.description: arXiv:2604.25997v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute the probability distribution for collisional energy loss of an ultrarelativistic parton crossing a quark-gluon plasma. This collisional quenching weight has not been determined previously, unlike the average collisional loss per unit distance, although it should be a more accurate quantity to use in jet-quenching phenomenology. The quenching weight is obtained from a well-known kinetic equation which resums an arbitrary number of elastic scatterings of the energetic parton with the medium, providing a complete description of the stochastic energy exchange, including the possibility of energy gain from thermal fluctuations. The formulation also naturally extends the standard treatment of collisional energy loss to finite path lengths, which could be relevant not only for heavy-ion collisions, but also for light-ion, and possibly proton-nucleus and proton-proton collisions. We predict the quenching weight in a setup where individual elastic scatterings are described using the hard thermal loop approximation for soft exchanges, with a smooth matching to the hard domain.
item.dc:creator: G. Jackson, S. Peign\'e

item.title: Particle species dependence of femtoscopic source parameters in high-energy nuclear collisions
item.description: arXiv:2605.26056v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: High-energy nuclear physics explores the properties of strongly interacting matter created in relativistic collisions of nuclei. Femtoscopy, a subfield of high-energy physics, utilizes quantum-statistical correlations of particles to characterize the space-time geometry of the particle-emitting source. Recent measurements and phenomenological investigations indicated that the shape of the source for identical pions can be well-described by L\'evy-stable distributions. The significant power-law tail of the pion source observed both in experiment and in simulations has been shown to originate from the process of L\'evy walk during the hadronic scattering phase of the collisions. To better understand the physical processes behind the formation of such power laws, an important next step is to investigate particle species dependence, especially the source shape of identical kaon and proton pairs. As a direct continuation of our previous studies, in this Letter, we present a detailed three-dimensional investigation of the two-particle source shape in simulations of Au+Au collisions at 200 GeV per nucleon pair collision energy using the EPOS3 model. We show the dependence of the extracted femtoscopic source parameters on particle species, centrality and average transverse mass. We find that the scale parameters do not show a clear transverse mass scaling between particle species, as there are systematic differences in the overlapping regions. The power-law exponents of pion and kaon pairs are compatible, while for protons it is higher, closer to the Gaussian limit. When new experimental measurements of kaon and proton correlations become available, these results will provide the basis of a data-model comparison.
item.dc:creator: D\'aniel Kincses, L\'aszl\'o Kov\'acs, M\'at\'e Csan\'ad

item.title: Critique of Breit-Wigner resonance scattering
item.description: arXiv:2605.28756v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the Breit-Wigner approach to scattering the phase shift $\delta$ is to have a form $\tan\delta_{\rm BW} =\Gamma_1/(E_1-E)$ at any real energy continuum scattering resonance. By analytic continuation this leads to complex energy poles in the scattering amplitude at $E_{\rm BW}=E_1-i\Gamma_1$, poles that are identified with unstable physical particles. By solving the square well scattering problem we identify some challenges to this approach. We find that setting $\tan\delta_{\rm BW} =\Gamma_1/(E_1-E)$ is not always a good description of the real energy continuum scattering amplitude, that $\Gamma_1$ can be negative, that $E_{\rm BW}$ is not in fact an energy eigenvalue, and thus cannot be identified with a physical particle. To address these issues we solve the square well Schr\"odinger problem and find explicit complex energy eigenvalues of the form $E_{PT}=E_2-i \Gamma_2$ due to the antilinear $PT$ (Parity, Time Reversal) symmetry of the Hamiltonian. However, $E_2\neq E_1$ and $\Gamma_2\neq \Gamma_1$. As Hamiltonian eigenstates with energy $E_{PT}=E_2-i \Gamma_2$ these states can be identified with physical particles and correspond to phase shifts of the form $\tan\delta_{PT} =\Gamma_2/(E_2-E)$. Then by analytic continuation to real energy they give the same real energy resonance shape as a standard Breit-Wigner. However, the determined positions and widths of these resonances should be associated with $E_2$ and $\Gamma_2$ rather than with $E_1$ and $\Gamma_1$. We thus recognize two forms of resonance in the real energy scattering amplitude $f(E)$, those associated with the continuum (the complex $E$ plane branch cut) and those due to poles in the complex $E$ plane. Only the latter can be associated with real particles. The continuum resonances are not associated with Breit-Wigner modes, and the number of such resonances correlates with the number of square well bound states.
item.dc:creator: Philip D. Mannheim

item.title: B Meson Semi-Invisible Decays via Perturbative QCD
item.description: arXiv:2606.07776v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper focuses on the dark sector decay processes of $B$ mesons ($B\to \mathcal{B}_8\ +$ invisible). Using the perturbative QCD (pQCD) approach, we calculate the upper bounds on the branching ratios for decays from $B$ mesons into light baryons and dark baryons within two distinct $B$-Mesogenesis scenarios. A detailed discussion of the form factor $B\to \mathcal{B}_8$ is presented. Based on the derived form factors and effective couplings, we then reach the final numerical analysis. The results show that these upper bounds can reach sizable, especially for $B^0\to n\psi$ in Type-I scenario, with values of orderis $\mathcal{O}(10^{-5})$ . Such processes are expected to facilitate the search for dark matter at hadron colliders and B factories.
item.dc:creator: Han-Bing Liu, Ye Xing, Bin Luo

item.title: Retarded Correlators of Charge Transport in a Magnetic Field
item.description: arXiv:2606.08139v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study charge transport in a magnetized relativistic plasma using kinetic theory within the relaxation-time approximation. By exactly solving the linearized Boltzmann equation in a uniform magnetic field, we obtain an analytic solution for the distribution function in terms of Bessel functions. Using this solution, we compute the full set of retarded current-current correlators and verify the Ward identities. In the hydrodynamic limit, we extract the charge diffusion modes, demonstrating that the transverse diffusion coefficient is strongly suppressed by the magnetic field, scaling as $1/B_0^2$ in the strong-field regime, while the longitudinal diffusion remains unaffected. Furthermore, we analyze the non-hydrodynamic branch cuts in the complex frequency plane, determining their kinematic thresholds and identifying the underlying wave-particle interactions as longitudinal Landau damping and transverse cyclotron damping.
item.dc:creator: Xuan Zhao, Qiuze Sun, Yi Wang, Jin Hu

item.title: Phenomenology of heavy-flavour jet angularities at hadron colliders
item.description: arXiv:2606.20798v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute resummed and matched predictions for jet angularities in hadronic Z+jet events, where the jet is initiated by a b-quark. The analysis is performed both with and without grooming the candidate jets using the SoftDrop algorithm. Mass effects are consistently included at both fixed-order and resummed levels. Our theoretical predictions also incorporate non-perturbative corrections from the underlying event and hadronization, implemented through parton-to-hadron transfer matrices extracted from dedicated Monte Carlo simulations with Sherpa. Finally, we compare results for b-jets with the ones from light-flavour jets, in order to quantify the impact of finite-mass effects.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Ghira, Lorenzo Mai, Simone Marzani, Daniel Reichelt, Steffen Schumann, Leon St\"ocker

item.title: Non-Standard Interactions and Light Z' Bosons from CEvNS Data at CONUS+
item.description: arXiv:2606.24005v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyze the first Conus+ reactor-antineutrino spectrum to constrain nonstandard neutrino interactions (NSI) with quarks and light vector $Z'$ mediators in $E_6$ and leptophilic $U(1)_{L_a-L_b}$ models. The prediction includes coherent elastic antineutrino--nucleus scattering (CEvNS) and elastic antineutrino--electron scattering (EvES), with Standard Model (SM)--mediator interference in each channel and an analytically profiled normalization uncertainty. We formulate $L_e-L_\mu$ and $L_e-L_\tau$ in a common charge convention, combining direct electron scattering with the nuclear interaction induced by photon-- $Z'$ mixing. The data remain compatible with the SM. Electronic scattering has little effect on the quark-NSI and fixed-coupling $E_6$ angular regions, but substantially strengthens the low-mass coupling limits of the $E_6$ benchmarks. The leptophilic models share a common low-mass plateau dominated by electronic scattering, while their limits separate at larger mediator masses through their different nuclear loop contributions.
item.dc:creator: Ch. M. Benavides, C. S. Mu\~noz, B. C. Canas, Eduardo Rojas

item.title: Neutron tagging of heavy lepton pair production at RHIC and LHC energies
item.description: arXiv:2607.11224v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We calculated cross sections for $\gamma\gamma \rightarrow \ell^+\ell^-$ ($\ell=e,\mu,\tau$) production in ultraperipheral gold and lead collisions and compare our results with recent measurements from the STAR, ALICE, ATLAS, and CMS experiments at center of mass energies $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200$ GeV, $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=2.76 $ TeV, and $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02$ TeV. The calculations are performed within lowest order quantum electrodynamics (LO QED) using a Monte Carlo technique for calculating the impact parameter dependent probability, and subsequently combined with neutron emission probabilities associated with Coulomb excitation of the nuclei. These neutron emission scenarios are modeled using a Poisson statistics, allowing the cross sections to be categorized into experimentally relevant neutron classes: 0n0n, 0nXn, XnXn, and inclusive (0n0n+0nXn+XnXn) production. To enable a direct comparison with experiments, fiducial phase space restrictions corresponding to the acceptance of each detector are implemented.
item.dc:creator: Atacan Fatih Candar, Mehmet Cem G\"u\c{c}l\"u

item.title: Beyond leading-logarithm photon production from two-loop diagrams in a hot QCD medium
item.description: arXiv:2607.24950v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate high-energy photon production from $2\leftrightarrow 2$ processes in a quark-gluon plasma by evaluating the imaginary part of the two-loop photon self-energies in thermal QCD. Working in the imaginary-time formalism, we derive analytical expressions for the leading-logarithmic and beyond-leading-logarithmic contributions to the photon production rate from $2\leftrightarrow 2$ processes. We retain the full Fermi--Dirac and Bose--Einstein statistical factors and compare the resulting Compton and annihilation rates with those obtained from kinetic theory and the closed-time-path formalism. The summed rates agree with the corresponding established results, providing a nontrivial consistency check of the calculation. Furthermore, when we consider the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution for incoming particles, we find that quantum corrections are absent in the individual $2\leftrightarrow 2$ processes. However, the total rate agrees with that of full statistics.
item.dc:creator: Sumit, Ritesh Ghosh, Munshi G. Mustafa

item.title: Dynamical flattening of halo density cusps by Q-ball dark matter
item.description: arXiv:2607.28517v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Cold, collisionless dark matter successfully explains a wide range of observations, including the formation of large-scale structure. Nevertheless, tensions remain on small, galactic scales, most notably the cusp-core, or inner-mass-deficit, problem and the diversity of inner rotation-curve shapes and central densities at fixed halo mass. These observations suggest that additional dark-sector physics may affect the inner structure of halos, although no generally accepted explanation has yet emerged. Here, making use of a toy but representative model, we investigate how interacting dark-matter Q-balls -- non-topological solitons stabilized by a conserved charge -- modify halo centers and generate a diversity of inner profiles. Our calculations include merger-induced mass and kinetic-energy losses, elastic heat transport, and the gravitational readjustment of the halo; flattening and later recontraction can both occur. Produced in the early Universe in the dark sector, these Q-balls grow in the dense central regions of halos, while their interaction cross section decreases as the soliton mass increases. This process operates preferentially in halo centers, converting part of the rest-mass energy stored in massive Q-balls into relativistic dark-sector particles and thereby modifying the inner mass-density profile. The resulting density-dependent energy loss competes with heat transport and halo response. An ensemble of initial assembly conditions yields very different final densities at fixed microphysics, although neither a universal constant-density core nor a statistical fit to the observed population is established.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Libanov, Sergey Troitsky

item.title: Heavy neutral leptons beyond the BBN bound: probing the lepton asymmetry of the Universe
item.description: arXiv:2608.10123v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Hadronically decaying particles with lifetimes $\tau\gtrsim0.02\,{\rm s}$ are excluded by Big Bang Nucleosynthesis almost independently of their abundance: the mesons from their decays convert protons into neutrons faster than the reverse, and helium is overproduced. For heavy neutral leptons (HNLs), this blankets the couplings the upcoming accelerator searches can reach. We propose a scenario with large lepton flavor asymmetries in which HNLs evade it. A Dirac HNL decays into $\pi^+$ and its antiparticle into $\pi^-$, so an asymmetry between the two populations injects an excess of $\pi^+$, which converts the neutrons back to their standard abundance, while a cancellation between the asymmetries and the HNL decays keeps the shift in $N_{\rm eff}$ small. This opens the parameter space with $m_l+m_\pi\lesssim m_N\lesssim1\,{\rm GeV}$ and $\tau_N\lesssim1\,{\rm s}$, including a substantial region within the reach of SHiP. A discovery there, combined with the BBN and CMB observables, would fix the primordial flavor asymmetries up to one remaining direction. The relic neutrino background and gravitational waves from the QCD transition epoch may probe that direction, and with it the lepton asymmetry of the Universe.
item.dc:creator: Kensuke Akita, Maksym Ovchynnikov, Vsevolod Syvolap

item.title: Enhanced Three-Particle Contribution to Electroweak Penguin $B$-Meson Decays
item.description: arXiv:2608.14341v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute for the first time the subleading twist correction to the exclusive rare $b \to \left \{s, d \right \} \ell^{+} \ell^{-}$ decays from the three-particle $B$-meson distribution amplitude at next-to-leading order accuracy by employing the soft-collinear effective theory. This constitutes the last missing ingredient for the complete factorization analysis of the hadronic matrix element of the weak effective Hamiltonian at leading power in the heavy quark expansion. Incorporating further a variety of the next-to-next-to-leading-order QCD corrections to the spectator-scattering amplitude and the weak annihilation topology, we then present the improved field-theoretic predictions for phenomenologically interesting observables in the electroweak penguin $B \to \left \{K, \pi \right \} \ell^{+} \ell^{-}$ decays.
item.dc:creator: Yong-Kang Huang, Yu-Ming Wang, Xue-Chen Zhao

item.title: Mixing-angle sensitivity of inclusive $\Xi_{bc} $ and $\Omega_{bc}$ lifetimes
item.description: arXiv:2609.00660v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the inclusive lifetimes of $\Xi_{bc}^{+}$, $\Xi_{bc}^{0}$, and $\Omega_{bc}^{0}$ with emphasis on the mixing between the spin-zero and spin-one $bc$-diquark configurations. The matrix elements are evaluated in both the homogeneous bag model (HBM) and the nonrelativistic quark model (NRQM). At the benchmark mixing angles $-23.0^\circ$ for $\Xi_{bc}$ and $-23.5^\circ$ for $\Omega_{bc}$, the corresponding lifetime triplets are $(\tau_{\Xi_{bc}^{+}},\tau_{\Xi_{bc}^{0}},\tau_{\Omega_{bc}^{0}})=(0.421^{+0.098}_{-0.093}{}^{+0.007}_{-0.014},0.075^{+0.035}_{-0.017}{}^{+0.004}_{-0.001},0.223^{+0.074}_{-0.046}{}^{+0.018}_{-0.012})\,\mathrm{ps}$ in HBM and $(\tau_{\Xi_{bc}^{+}},\tau_{\Xi_{bc}^{0}},\tau_{\Omega_{bc}^{0}})=(0.367^{+0.076}_{-0.070}{}^{+0.001}_{-0.005},0.100^{+0.032}_{-0.014}{}^{+0.006}_{-0.001},0.229^{+0.066}_{-0.042}{}^{+0.017}_{-0.011})\,\mathrm{ps}$ in NRQM. The first errors are the fixed-angle uncertainties; the second are the envelopes from varying each mixing angle by $\pm10^\circ$ with all other inputs fixed. Relative to the unmixed spin-one reference points, the $\Xi_{bc}^{0}$ and $\Omega_{bc}$ lifetimes decrease by approximately $17\%$-$19\%$. Neither the minimum nor the maximum of the central lifetime curves occurs at a pure $S_{bc}=0$ or $S_{bc}=1$ configuration; the extrema instead lie at mixed angles with $|\phi_{{\cal B}}|\simeq27^\circ$-$63^\circ$. The two pure-spin cases alone are therefore insufficient to characterize the angular dependence.
item.dc:creator: Hai-Yang Cheng, Chia-Wei Liu, Fanrong Xu

item.title: Forward BFKL evolution at fixed coupling as a random walk, and the loss of its probability law at fixed next-to-leading order
item.description: arXiv:2609.18269v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The BFKL equation describes how the density of gluons in a hadron grows with the collision energy. This evolution is often treated as a random walk in the logarithm of the gluon transverse momentum, but it has not been established that one set of positive step probabilities describes this walk in the size and the direction of the momentum, or that such probabilities exist beyond leading order. We show that one positive step density describes the evolution in the size and the direction of the momentum with no approximation at leading order, fixed coupling and zero momentum transfer, once the gluon density is rescaled by the size of its transverse momentum and its growth is divided out. The displacements of the resulting walk over separate, equal intervals of rapidity, the logarithm of the energy in units of a reference energy, are then independent and identically distributed, which makes the walk a Levy process. We also show that this description fails when the series in the coupling is cut at next-to-leading order, with the reference energy and the scale of the coupling both set by the product of the transverse momenta before and after an emission. The evolution averaged over directions then has no probability law at any fixed positive coupling and rapidity, because a negative correction growing as the squared logarithm of the momentum ratio outweighs the leading term when one momentum is much larger than the other. A positive step density for the averaged walk agrees with this truncated evolution to next-to-leading order and defines a random walk for every value of the strong coupling below one, so the failure comes from the truncation. The main message is that agreement with perturbation theory does not guarantee positive step probabilities, so an evolution equation summed to all orders and meant to describe a random walk must be tested for them.
